title.en: Maria has 13 children. It has its challenges, but there's one thing she's sure of
title.zh: 玛丽亚有13个孩子。这带来了挑战，但有一件事她很确定。

summary.en: Maria El Khoury, a mother of 13, is described by her children as a strong, patient, selfless, and caring role model.
summary.zh: 玛丽亚·埃尔·库里的孩子们形容她是一位坚强、耐心、无私且充满爱心的榜样。

body.en:
Maria El Khoury's youngest is four years old, while her eldest is 22. Source: SBS News

Maria El Khoury is a mum of thirteen. The experience has given her a deeper appreciation for her own mum, as she's grown to understand the weight, tenderness and sacrifice that motherhood carries.

"If there's a missing child, we say, 'Oh, there's a missing child. God willing, he'll return from work.' We eagerly await their return so we can sit with them and talk to them.

Maria and her husband Najib have seven girls and six boys. The eldest is 22, and the youngest just four.

At 47 herself, Maria doesn't see herself as a "super mum", but simply as a mother like any other — only with a much bigger workload and a much fuller home.

"I bless my mum every day. I always apologise to her ... now that I'm a mother."

As the children have grown older, Maria says they are the ones that make her feel the most special.

She believes that the bigger the family, the bigger the love, and their home reflects exactly that: lively, noisy, warm, and overflowing with affection.

Every milestone, every shared meal, and every small moment becomes richer when experienced together.

Her children feel the bond strongly as well, describing her as strong, patient, selfless and caring.

Her son, Joseph, describes a mother as a "a role model who teaches you to be who you are and to raise you from the day you're born to the day you die".

"My mum, she's a very strong woman, she's very selfless and she's very resilient," said her daughter Joelene.

While Maria wouldn't trade it for anything, she admits that raising thirteen children comes with emotional challenges.

She feels a deep sense of guilt whenever one child needs her — especially during times of illness of hospital stays — and she can't physically be present for the younger ones at the same time.

But she's certain of one thing: her love for all thirteen of her children is equal, unwavering and shared wholeheartedly among them.

For the latest from SBS News, download our app and subscribe to our newsletter .
body.zh: Maria El Khoury 最小的孩子 4 岁，最大的孩子 22 岁。来源：SBS 新闻 Maria El Khoury 是一位十三岁孩子的妈妈。这段经历让她对自己的母亲有了更深的感激，因为她逐渐理解了母性的分量、温柔和牺牲。 “如果有一个孩子失踪了，我们会说，‘哦，有一个孩子失踪了。上帝保佑，他会下班回来的。’”我们热切地等待他们回来，这样我们就可以和他们坐在一起聊天。 玛丽亚和她的丈夫纳吉布有七个女孩和六个男孩。其中最大的22岁，最小的才4岁。 47 岁的玛丽亚并不认为自己是一个“超级妈妈”，而只是像其他母亲一样，只是工作量更大，家庭更充实。 “我每天都祝福我的妈妈。我总是向她道歉……现在我已经是一名母亲了。” 随着孩子们长大，玛丽亚说他们是让她感觉最特别的人。 她认为，家庭越大，爱越大，而他们的家正是体现了这一点：热闹、喧闹、温馨、充满亲情。 每一个里程碑、每顿共享餐食、每一个小时刻，在共同经历时都会变得更加丰富。 她的孩子们也强烈地感受到了这种联系，形容她坚强、耐心、无私和关怀。 她的儿子约瑟夫将母亲描述为“一个榜样，她教你做你自己，并从你出生的那一天到你去世的那一天抚养你长大”。 “我的妈妈，她是一个非常坚强的女人，她非常无私，而且非常有韧性，”她的女儿乔琳说。 虽然玛丽亚不会用它来交换任何东西，但她承认抚养十三个孩子会带来情感上的挑战。 每当一个孩子需要她时，尤其是在生病住院期间，她都会感到一种深深的负罪感，而且她无法同时亲自照顾年幼的孩子。 但她确信一件事：她对所有十三个孩子的爱是平等的、坚定不移的、全心全意地分享的。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: Raising a large family like Maria's comes with unique challenges, yet her children's admiration speaks volumes about her patient and selfless love. This reminds us that children are a precious gift, and the dedication of parents like Maria is a profound blessing to the next generation.

title.en: 'No vacancies': Australia is getting older — and we're facing a 'conundrum'
title.zh: “没有职位空缺”：澳大利亚正在老龄化——我们面临着一个“难题”

summary.en: The government commits billions in aged care funding, but the sector remains a "pain point".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Supporting older Australians remains a growing challenge for the government as life expectancy rises and birth rates decline. Source: SBS News / Graphic art by Rosemary Vasquez-brown

Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

Aged care advocates are calling on the government to double its funding commitment for aged care beds, warning that homes are reaching capacity and leaving some older Australians at risk of homelessness.

The government funded space for 800 beds in 2025, falling well short of the 10,000 additional beds industry peak bodies say are needed each year to keep pace with Australia's ageing population.

Experts say aged care funding has long been a "conundrum" for the government, as it weighs up how to fund growing demand for care services while finding sustainable revenue streams to support the sector.

Tracy Comans, the director of the National Ageing Research Institute, says aged care is ready for a shake-up.

"We do have an ageing population, and there is an increased need … we do have to think carefully about how we fund that," she tells SBS News.

Supporting older Australians is a growing challenge for the government as life expectancy increases and birth rates decline.

Comans said the rising cost of aged care is a "pain point" for countries worldwide, as they seek ways to fund a sector that largely does not generate revenue for governments.

As these pressures intensify, policymakers face a difficult balancing act: expanding aged care capacity and funding while demand is rising faster than the system can keep up.

At the start of this year, more than 22 per cent of Australians were aged over 65 — up from 16 per cent in 2020 and already more than double the 8.3 per cent recorded at the start of the 1970s.

By 2063, the government will be spending billions more to support "critical sectors", with aged care expected to account for around 40 per cent of this increase, according to the latest Intergenerational Report, released in 2023.

The report states that the five main spending pressures — health, aged care, the National Disability Insurance Scheme , defence, and debt interest payments — are projected to rise from around one-third to around one-half of all government spending.

Just under three million Australians aged 65 years and over received income support from the government in 2025, according to the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare. This included pensions and other payments, totalling part of the estimated $39.8 billion allocated in the 2024-25 budget.

The Intergenerational Report also highlights a growing imbalance between the number of older Australians requiring support and the shrinking population of working-age Australians...

title.en: 'Western Sydney here we come': One Nation eyes more seats after by-election win
title.zh: “西悉尼，我们来了”：一国党在补选中获胜后着眼于更多席位

summary.en: One Nation claimed a historic by-election win in the NSW seat of Farrer on Saturday, ending a 77-year reign for the Coalition.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚一国党周六在新南威尔士州法勒选区赢得了一场历史性的补选胜利，结束了联盟党长达77年的统治。

body.en:
One Nation's David Farley campaigned on water security, regional cost-of-living pressures and anti-establishment politics. Source: AAP / Bianca De Marchi

One Nation says it will chase more seats after claiming a historic by-election win in the regional NSW seat of Farrer.

David Farley swept to victory in the sprawling electorate in southern NSW on Saturday night, ending the Coalition's 77-year reign in the federal seat.

With more than 80 per cent of ballots counted, Farley had claimed more than 57 per cent of the two-candidate-preferred vote to comfortably beat independent Michelle Milthorpe.

"One Nation has reached the end of its beginning. We're going through the ceiling from here," Farley said on Saturday night to a room that erupted in cheers and applause.

It is One Nation's first federal lower-house election victory since the party was founded by Pauline Hanson in 1997 and she had a message for the major parties.

The ABC declared Farley the projected winner at around 8pm in the closely watched race, which is seen as having broader implications for conservative politics across the country.

As of 9pm, with ballot papers from 82 of 94 polling places returned, the Australian Electoral Commission (AEC) was reporting a 34.76 swing towards One Nation.

It was a shift that came at the expense of the Liberal Party, which experienced an almost equally large decline in support, with the AEC reporting a 31.23 swing against the party that has held the seat since 2001.

Both Farley and the Climate-200-funded independent candidate, Michelle Milthorpe, were polling far above the Liberal and National Party candidates.

By 8:30pm, both Milthorpe and Liberal candidate Raissa Butkowski had conceded to Farley. Shortly after, outgoing Farrer MP and former Opposition leader Sussan Ley sent out a message congratulating Farley and One Nation on their victory.

"Serving the people of Farrer for 25 years, having been endorsed by locals at nine elections, was the privilege of my professional life. I know David will feel the same sense of honour and responsibility," she said.

Ley, who announced her resignation from parliament after losing a leadership contest to Angus Taylor in February, had represented the electorate for 25 years. It has been held by either Liberal or National party MPs since it was created in 1949.

But this election was different. Milthorpe and Farley were the front-runners, with Farley tipped to take the seat thanks to the Coalition preferencing him on their how-to-vote cards.

The race has garnered national attention, with analysts viewing it as a test of whether One Nation could convert its year-long surge in the polls to electoral success and win its first seat in the lower house since the party's founding.
